chunks: Rijal al-Kashshi: Muhammad ibn Mas'ud, from Muhammad ibn Nusayr, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Abd al-Aziz ibn al-Muhtadi who said:

I said to Abi al-Hasan al-Ridha (peace be upon him): May I be your ransom, I cannot always reach you to ask you all that which I need from the teachings of my religion, is Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman trustworthy (thiqa) and can I take from him what I need from the teachings of my religion? He said: Yes.

key_terms.أَبِي الْحَسَنِ الرِّضَا: Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (Imam al-Rida, the 8th Imam)
key_terms.ثِقَةٌ: Trustworthy (a technical term in Rijal indicating a narrator's reliability)

ai.seo_question: Is Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman considered a trustworthy narrator in Shia hadith sciences?
ai.summary: Abd al-Aziz ibn al-Muhtadi seeks clarification from Imam al-Rida regarding the reliability of Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman as a primary source for religious knowledge, highlighting the Imam's role in validating the chain of transmission during a period of scholarly transition. The Imam’s affirmative response confirms Yunus’s trustworthiness (thiqa), establishing his narrations as authoritative for deriving religious rulings and guiding the community in the absence of direct, constant access to the Imam.

en.ammaar-muslim: 5. [5/286] Rijal al-Kashshi: Muhammad b. Masud from Muhammad b. Nusayr from Muhammad b. Isa from Abd al-Aziz b. al-Muhtadi who said:

I said to Abi al-Hasan al-Ridha عليه السلام: May I be made your ransom - I cannot always reach you to ask you all that which I need from the teachings of my religion, is Yunus b. Abd al-Rahman Thiqa (trustworthy) and can I take from him what I need from the teachings of my religion? He said: Yes.
